sentences.text: Tenontosaurus was a medium-sized ornithopod that weighed roughly 1000 kg, though estimates range up to 2 tons.
Its mouth featured a thick, U-shaped beak created by flaring premaxillae, while the lower jaw ended in a predentary bone unique to ornithischians.
Every tooth in this animal was enameled on only the inner or medial surface.
The skull itself was low and long, appearing very elongated when viewed from above.
Its spine consisted of twelve cervical vertebrae, fifteen dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and at least sixty-one tail vertebrae.
Populations of this animal increased dramatically during a shift from arid to wetter climates, proving it was remarkably adaptable.
Like Tyrannosaurus and Allosaurus, one individual died at eight years old without reaching full adult size.
The first fossil was found in 1903 in Big Horn County, Montana, by an AMNH expedition.
Barnum Brown informally named the creature 'Tenantosaurus' or 'sinew lizard' because of its stiffening tendons.
The genus Tenontosaurus was officially named by John Ostrom in 1970.
Later, Jonathan Tennant described the postcranial skeleton in 2013 using specimen LL.12275, and the skull was detailed in 2015 using specimen OMNH 58340 found in 2000.
This dinosaur was a facultative quadruped capable of standing on two or four legs, though it likely could not move rapidly on four.
As a low browser, an adult could reach a maximum height of about 3 meters when standing bipedally to feed.
It possessed a powerful U-shaped beak and angled teeth that allowed it to consume leaves, wood, and fruit.
Medullary bone tissue found in a specimen indicates it used this tissue for reproduction, suggesting early-diverging lineages reached maturity before maximum size.
The presence of medullary bone in the femur and tibia confirms the use of this tissue, found today only in egg-laying birds, for reproduction.
Fossil teeth and skeletons of the theropod Deinonychus are frequently found associated with Tenontosaurus tilletti remains, with about 20% of fossils found near the predator.
Tenontosaurus is classified as a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.
It was originally placed in the family Iguanodontidae but later reclassified into Hypsilophodontidae.
Although its light structure resembles a hypsilophodontid, detailed examination suggests it is likely a basal member of Iguanodontia.
Tenontosaurus lived during the middle Cretaceous period, between approximately 122 and 108 million years ago.
It lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian stages, between 121.4 and 93.9 million years ago.
The animal inhabited a paleoenvironment of tropical or sub-tropical forests, floodplains, and swamps similar to modern-day Louisiana.
When the animal first appeared in Wyoming and Montana, the climate was arid to semi-arid with seasonal rainfall and occasional droughts.
In the Cloverly Formation, Tenontosaurus was the most abundant vertebrate, five times more common than the next most frequent species, Sauropelta.
In the arid Little Sheep Mudstone Member, it was the sole herbivorous dinosaur, sharing its habitat with Deinonychus, an allosauroid theropod, and a goniopholid crocodile.
It is debated whether Ostrom's original reconstruction of the Tenontosaurus skull accurately represented its true depth.
The position of Tenontosaurus in the evolutionary tree was very problematic and controversial due to a lack of adequate cladistic analysis.
